name: Bytebot

modes.label: Self-hosted open-source Docker desktop agent
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Self-hosted Apache-2.0 software
plans.note: No Bytebot licensing fee, subscription or software usage limit. Customer pays its own Docker/Kubernetes/Railway/AWS/GCP/Azure infrastructure and chosen LLM API. Concurrency is limited by deployed hardware/task queues, not a published hosted quota.

caveats: Public product boots sandboxed desktops for multi-app agents, with browser, filesystem, terminal and mouse/keyboard/screenshot control; open-source container also available. YC marks acquired, not necessarily dead. No hosted resource tariff verified.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
Self-host reference resources: development 2 CPU / 4 GB RAM, production 4+ CPU / 8+ GB; the desktop container uses ~1 GB idle, 2 GB+ active.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

status: archived: official GitHub repository read-only since 2026-03-07; YC lists the company as acquired; website/docs still online

own_agent_api.quote: The Agent API runs on port 9991 and provides high-level task management:
own_agent_api.note: Tasks API: POST /tasks with a natural-language description (+ file upload), GET /tasks/:id and /:id/messages, POST /:id/messages (follow-up), /:id/takeover, /:id/resume, /:id/cancel, WebSocket real-time updates. Harnesses: Bytebot's own computer-use agent (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini or LiteLLM models) and, in the GitHub repo (not in docs), a Claude Code variant 'bytebot-agent-cc' (docker-compose-claude-code.yml) built on '@anthropic-ai/claude-code' query(). The agent runs in its own container and drives the desktop container over its API.

harness_api.quote: The Agent API runs on port 9991 and provides high-level task management:
harness_api.note: Tasks API: POST /tasks with a natural-language description (+ file upload), GET /tasks/:id and /:id/messages, POST /:id/messages (follow-up), /:id/takeover, /:id/resume, /:id/cancel, WebSocket real-time updates. Harnesses: Bytebot's own computer-use agent (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini or LiteLLM models) and, in the GitHub repo (not in docs), a Claude Code variant 'bytebot-agent-cc' (docker-compose-claude-code.yml) built on '@anthropic-ai/claude-code' query(). The agent runs in its own container and drives the desktop container over its API.

ingress_rules.quote: No authentication by default (localhost only). Supports REST and MCP.
ingress_rules.note: No built-in access control layer: the Desktop API (9990, incl. noVNC) and Agent API (9991) have no auth in the code; exposure is only whatever Docker port mappings or the optional Helm Ingress you configure. Helm 'auth'/'networkPolicy' values shown in the docs do not exist in the chart.

guest_firewall.note: Desktop container runs privileged (docker-compose and Helm securityContext) with passwordless sudo ('Sudo Access: Yes (passwordless)'), so iptables/nftables in its own network namespace should work. Not tested.

secret_proxy.quote: Bytebot can handle authentication automatically - including passwords, 2FA, and even complex multi-step authentication flows - when you set up a password manager extension.
secret_proxy.note: Website credentials live in a password-manager extension (1Password/Bitwarden) inside the desktop, so real secrets enter the sandbox. LLM keys sit in the separate agent container or the optional bundled LiteLLM proxy (bytebot-llm-proxy), never in the desktop, but that is an architecture split, not a credential-injecting proxy for the sandbox.

volume_attach.note: Helm chart option desktop.persistence (PVC, default disabled, 10Gi, ReadWriteOnce, mounted at /data). Self-hosted, so this is your own K8s/Docker storage; no hosted volume product.

isolation.quote: The Bytebot Desktop Environment (also called Bytebot Core) is a complete Linux desktop that runs in a Docker container.

docker_inside.quote: Pre-installed Software ... Text editor, Office tools, PDF viewer, File manager ... Thunderbird email client, Terminal emulator ... 1Password password manager, Visual Studio Code (VSCode), Git version control, Python 3 environment
docker_inside.note: Docker is not listed among the pre-installed software inside the desktop container, and the container itself already runs privileged for input/automation, not documented as offering nested container runtimes.

nested_virt.quote: Runs completely isolated from your host system
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the desktop runs as a plain Docker container (isolation=container), with no /dev/kvm or nested-VM capability documented.

anti_bot.quote: Bytebot is an open-source AI agent that can control a computer desktop to complete tasks for you. It runs in Docker containers on your own infrastructure
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Bytebot is a self-hosted desktop-automation agent (uses a real Firefox on a real desktop) with no documented stealth/fingerprint-evasion feature against bot detection.

captcha_solving.quote: Bytebot can handle authentication automatically - including passwords, 2FA, and even complex multi-step authentication flows - when you set up a password manager extension.
captcha_solving.note: Docs describe password/2FA autofill via password-manager browser extensions, not automated CAPTCHA solving; no CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented.

ssh.quote: Navigate to `http://localhost:9990/vnc` for instant access ... No software installation required
ssh.note: not offered: documented access paths to the desktop container are the noVNC web viewer, REST API, and MCP endpoint; no SSH server/access is documented (K8s/Docker users could `kubectl exec`/`docker exec`, but that is generic container tooling, not a Bytebot SSH feature).

snapshot.quote: Easy Reset: Destroy and recreate in seconds ... Clean Workspace: Each restart provides a fresh environment
snapshot.note: No snapshot/checkpoint API is documented; restart gives a fresh container, not a saved state.

snapshot_auto.quote: Each restart provides a fresh environment
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: no automatic state save/restore on stop documented.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: The Agent API runs on port 9991 and provides high-level task management
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint exists in the documented API reference (only task create/list/message/takeover/resume/cancel).

fork.quote: The Agent API runs on port 9991 and provides high-level task management
fork.note: No clone/fork-machine API documented; you could manually spin up another docker-compose/Helm instance, but that is generic infra, not a Bytebot feature.

fork_running.quote: The Agent API runs on port 9991 and provides high-level task management
fork_running.note: No fork/clone capability at all is documented (see fork).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The Agent API runs on port 9991 and provides high-level task management
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork or memory-snapshot capability documented at all.

pause_resume.quote: Take control of the desktop when you need to guide or assist Bytebot
pause_resume.note: Bytebot has a task-level 'takeover'/'resume' concept (human pauses the AGENT's actions, not the machine), not a pause/resume of the container itself with billing effect; self-hosted has no billing concept anyway.

wake_on_request.quote: It runs in Docker containers on your own infrastructure
wake_on_request.note: not offered: self-hosted containers stay in whatever state (running/stopped) the customer's own orchestrator leaves them in; no documented auto-wake-on-request feature.

volume_shared.quote: desktop.persistence (PVC, default disabled, 10Gi, ReadWriteOnce, mounted at /data)
volume_shared.note: Documented persistence is a single-desktop PVC set to ReadWriteOnce; no shared-volume-across-multiple-running-desktops feature is documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Persistent Environment: Install programs and they stay available for future tasks
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: self-hosted containers run via `restart: unless-stopped` / Kubernetes Deployments and are managed by the customer's own orchestrator, not an idle-based auto-stop feature of Bytebot.

live_resize.quote: Adjust resources based on your needs: desktop: resources: requests: memory: "2Gi" cpu: "1" limits: memory: "4Gi" cpu: "2"
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are set via static Helm/Docker resource requests/limits edited in config, with no documented live-resize-without-recreate API.

agent_harnesses.quote: bytebot-agent-cc: build: context: ../packages/ dockerfile: bytebot-agent-cc/Dockerfile ... ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}
agent_harnesses.note: GitHub repo ships an alternate docker-compose stack running a Claude Code-based agent ('bytebot-agent-cc', built on '@anthropic-ai/claude-code') as a drop-in harness driving the same desktop container, alongside Bytebot's own default computer-use agent.

lang_node.quote: bytebotd Daemon - The automation service built on nutjs that executes computer actions
lang_node.note: The desktop daemon (bytebotd) and agent/UI services are all Node.js/TypeScript (NestJS, Next.js, nutjs); Node.js is present in the runtime images, though not separately advertised as a user-facing 'pre-installed language' like Python 3 is.

public_ipv4.quote: It runs in Docker containers on your own infrastructure
public_ipv4.note: not offered: self-hosted, so any public IPv4 exposure comes entirely from the customer's own hosting (Railway, cloud VM, k8s LoadBalancer), not from Bytebot.

inbound_https.quote: ui: ingress: enabled: true hostname: bytebot.your-domain.com tls: true
inbound_https.note: HTTPS ingress is an optional Helm Ingress the customer configures on their own Kubernetes cluster (their own TLS/cert-manager/DNS), not a feature Bytebot itself provisions.

egress_allowlist.quote: Runs completely isolated from your host system
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: no provider-side outbound allow/deny-list or no-internet mode is documented; the desktop's egress is only whatever the customer's own Docker/K8s network policy allows.

egress_http_rules.quote: Runs completely isolated from your host system
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress rule feature is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: It runs in Docker containers on your own infrastructure
static_egress_ip.note: not offered as a Bytebot feature: any fixed outbound IP would come from the customer's own hosting setup, not from Bytebot itself.

gpu.quote: XFCE4 Desktop: Lightweight, responsive desktop environment
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Bytebot is a lightweight XFCE desktop-automation container with no documented GPU machine option.

windows.quote: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS: Stable, well-supported Linux distribution
windows.note: not offered: only a Linux (Ubuntu) desktop container is offered.

macos.quote: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS: Stable, well-supported Linux distribution
macos.note: not offered: only a Linux (Ubuntu) desktop container is offered.

byoc.quote: Why Self-Host Bytebot? ... Your tasks and data never leave your infrastructure. Everything runs locally on your servers.
byoc.note: not offered: Bytebot is self-hosted open-source software the customer deploys and operates themselves; there is no vendor-managed BYOC deployment offering (the vendor/company itself is archived/acquired).

soc2.quote: Bytebot - Desktop agents that use computers like a human — at cloud scale.
soc2.note: not offered: no SOC 2 attestation is mentioned anywhere on the site/docs; there is no hosted service to certify since the product is self-hosted OSS.

hipaa.quote: Bytebot - Desktop agents that use computers like a human — at cloud scale.
hipaa.note: not offered: no HIPAA/BAA program is documented; self-hosted OSS with no vendor-run service to sign a BAA for.

sso.note: not offered: the product ships with no built-in authentication layer at all, let alone SAML/OIDC SSO.

eu_data_residency.quote: It runs in Docker containers on your own infrastructure ... Your tasks and data never leave your infrastructure. Everything runs locally on your servers.
eu_data_residency.note: Since Bytebot is self-hosted software with no vendor-side data plane, customers can trivially run it entirely within EU infrastructure of their choosing; this is inherent to self-hosting rather than a distinct provider-managed region feature.

max_session_h.quote: Persistent Environment: Install programs and they stay available for future tasks
max_session_h.note: Self-hosted with `restart: unless-stopped` containers/Kubernetes Deployments; no documented maximum session duration or forced stop — it runs until the customer stops it.

egress_ip_type.quote: Railway provides a zero-ops PaaS experience with private networking ... All internal traffic flows through Railway's private networking. Only bytebot-ui is assigned a public domain.
egress_ip_type.note: Bytebot is self-hosted software with no vendor-run network of its own; official deployment guides target Railway PaaS, Kubernetes/Helm, and Docker, plus the plan note lists AWS/GCP/Azure as customer infrastructure — all standard cloud/datacenter hosting. No residential or mobile IP option is documented anywhere; outbound IP type is whatever datacenter the customer deploys into.

arm64.note: The published ghcr.io/bytebot-ai/bytebot-desktop:edge multi-arch image manifest list includes an arm64/linux platform image alongside amd64, so the desktop container runs on ARM64 hosts (e.g. Apple Silicon Docker, ARM Kubernetes nodes) out of the box.
